narration: Right now, you're walking into the most expensive six weeks of the year. Seventy-three percent of Americans will fund it entirely on credit.
visual: Dark background with countdown calendar to Christmas, credit card center stage with '$1,463' debt counter animating upward from zero

narration: Here's the thing — you're not overspending because you're generous. Retailers deliberately engineer holiday guilt, and it's worth twenty-three billion dollars to them.
visual: Light background with three gift boxes containing dollar signs popping in one by one, '$23 BILLION' label appears below

narration: Seventy-three percent of Americans use credit to fund the holidays. The average balance they're carrying into January is fourteen hundred and sixty-three dollars.
visual: Dark background with large credit card SVG, animated 73% progress bar filling left to right, balance counter counting up to $1,463

narration: By February, most people are still paying for December. The average holiday debt doesn't get paid off until April — four full months of interest.
visual: Light background with four calendar icons for January through April, each showing a dollar sign with a downward arrow draining

narration: And here's the kicker — this cycle plays out every year without fail. Retailers are already engineering next November's spending right now.
visual: Dark background with circular spinning arrows showing the annual loop: NOV, DEC, JAN-APR, OCT labeled around the cycle

narration: Set your gift cap before you even open the shopping app — not after. Families who do this keep four hundred and ten dollars in their pockets.
visual: Light background with piggy bank growing in size, savings counter animating to $410, text overlay 'Set Your Limit BEFORE You Shop'
